title: superclaude-starts-itself
owner: CC (code + proofs); Akien (the intention, and the scope ruling of 2026-07-30: 'import root + the verb', build-minimal, deferring host-seam verification and repair to a later rung)
intention: THE LAUNCHER BRINGS UP THE FLOOR IT NEEDS, THEN TELLS CLAUDE WHAT IT COULD NOT FIX. superclaude stops being a thing that only starts Claude Code and becomes the thing that starts Claude Code WITH AS MANY OF THE PARTS ALREADY WORKING AS IT CAN MANAGE: a venv in instance-space, an editable install so `cairn` imports from any directory, and every declared dependency actually present. Whatever it cannot repair rides into the session on --append-system-prompt, complete enough to act on, so the session opens already knowing rather than discovering. And the question that started it — 'how do I run a proof here?' — gets an ADDRESS: `cairn test`, registered with the dispatcher that already lists its own verbs.
why: Akien, 2026-07-30, watching a session burn four tool calls finding out how to run one proof: 'we're not selecting a pre-built venv before getting started... so if a venv is not built, you spend tokens sorting that over and over. Tokens spent and not compiled.' And on the report half: 'it does what it can, then reports to claude if there are problems so Claude can get them fixed. it's part of the tool becomes invisible when you use it.' Both halves are Law 1: an answered question that did not become structure gets re-derived, and re-derivation is the defect — whether the re-deriver is a human or the next session.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled) — the whole ticket
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured) — the floor is verified by importing, never assumed from a stamp
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics) — the undeclared-import rule became a proof, not prose
Law 7 (loud at diagnostic surfaces, permanent in records of truth) — the verb reports and seals nothing
the rescue ethos (launchers/intention+why.json) — the tier below the machinery, which must work when the machinery does not

proves_green.BUILDME: the seam exists, is sourced by superclaude, and cannot abort a launch
proves_green.PROVEME: launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py (14 cases) and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_cli.py (8 cases) both green, and the whole suite no worse than before

falsifier.proves_red: The floor can be reported UP while `import cairn` from outside the repo actually fails; OR the preflight can prevent Claude Code from starting; OR `cairn test` can report green without a proof having actually passed (including green over ZERO proofs).
falsifier.horizon: A host-seam's seal EXPIRES by construction — the venv lives where git cannot see it, so the host drifts with nothing in this repo changing. launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py IS the re-runnable verify; a green means the floor was up when it last ran, not that it is up now.

questions.a: A DOCSTRING IS NOT AN ADDRESS. The answer to 'how do I run a proof' was correctly written down — inside the proof file, which you can only read once you have already found it, which is the thing you were trying to do. Compiling an answer means putting it where the question is ASKED (the dispatcher), not where the answer is true.

A PROBE IS FOR A QUESTION THAT NEEDS TIME; A PROOF IS FOR ONE THAT DOES NOT. The undeclared-import rule was a candidate watch and became a proof instead — it is deterministically answerable from files in git, so watching for it would be waiting to discover something already knowable.
A VENV IS RUNTIME STATE. It went to ~/.cairn, never the repo. The tell is decisive and general: a thing that would need gitignoring is a thing in the wrong root.

A HINT THAT NAMES A CAUSE IT DID NOT MEASURE IS WORSE THAN SILENCE. Measured 2026-07-30: the venv-create finding read 'usually the missing ensurepip package' while the actual error was ENOENT on the parent directory. Now the measured output leads and everything after it is labelled a candidate — and there is a regression case pinning that.

REPRODUCIBILITY OVER OFFLINE CLEVERNESS. --system-site-packages was considered and refused: it would have satisfied psycopg2 from the host with no download, but it makes the floor's contents a function of what the box happens to have — the exact hypothesis that caused the defect.

THE FIRST LIVE FIRE MEASURED THE TEST SUITE, NOT THE WORLD (2026-07-30). The probe's very first pulse against the real boot log reported a floor that had ridden UNFIXED through TWELVE separate launches — a poke the owner would have had no reason to doubt. The finding was 'SYNTHETIC FINDING for the proof': launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py's own fixture, written twelve times by twelve runs of the suite, because the harness inherited the environment and bootstrap.sh writes to ${CAIRN_BOOT_LOG:-$HOME/.cairn/logs/boot}. The predicates were right, the reader was right, and the answer was fabricated. THE SAME SHAPE AS THE HOME-FIELD DEFECT watchme-emits-a-probe paid for hours earlier — the author's own artefacts counted as independent evidence — reached this time through a channel nobody was watching: a test that WRITES to a production diagnostic surface. Fixed at the source: the harness owns its own namespace (which is the recorder's design working, not an exception to it), and the containment tooth is STRUCTURAL — every child must go through _env() — because the first version grepped for one remembered fixture string and missed six more records from the other fixture in the same file. The record was decontaminated, with the removal recorded IN the record and the pre-image kept outside the namespace directory.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [WATCHME(reported-but-unfixed-floor):waiting] -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: Every ground_loop pulse reaching launchers' watcher. The probe reads ONE FILE — the boot namespace at ~/.cairn/logs/boot (or $CAIRN_BOOT_LOG), written by launchers/bootstrap.sh + launchers/superclaude through bin/logger_for_bash. No device, no bus, no network. A LAUNCH IS A PID (superclaude is one process per launch, and every record carries its pid), so launches need no counter and a concurrent shell's records separate themselves. It counts, per distinct `report: unfixed — <finding>` text, how many separate launches carried it. FIRES when >= 5 launches reported something AND some finding survived >= 3 launches. Three, not two: the second launch is often the same session that was just told and is still working; by the third the report has been in front of a session twice and the floor is still down.
watchme.enough: CLEARED once >= 5 launches have reported something AND nothing survived to the patience line — the reported-to-Claude path demonstrably closes, and a standing watch on a settled question is the re-derivation Law 1 refuses. THE FLOOR (5) IS ON BOTH PREDICATES and is >= the patience (3) on purpose: a floor below the patience would leave a corpus where the watch CLEARS but could never have FIRED — zero reports, zero survivors, question never asked — which is exactly the shape watchme-emits-a-probe's own probe shipped with and paid for on 2026-07-30. If the loop later stops closing, that is a NEW watch.
watchme.carrier: A dict carried by the probe's `carry`: the finding that would not die, how many launches it rode, the counts, and the `--no-preflight` bypass count beside it. THE BYPASS IS THE SHARPER SIGNAL and rides in the datum rather than in the predicate — it means someone routed around the floor check, but one bypass is a legitimate rescue, which is what the hatch is for, so the owner weighs it rather than the trigger. A POINTER to this ticket, never a copy (Law 6).
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the seam's reporting half is a bet on a human-and-model loop no proof can reach; a bet that did not pay belongs with the other buried predictions.
watchme.consumer: AKIEN, through the owner's gate. Re-opening this node because its intention did not work is the owner's act at the register; the probe has no authority to back-edge anything (Law 6).

filed_edges: CLOSED 2026-07-30 — INSTANCE-SPACE PROBE, BUILT. Was: 'the preflight writes ~/.cairn/logs/preflight.json on every launch and nothing reads it.' The boot now writes a per-launch trail to ~/.cairn/logs/boot via bin/logger_for_bash, and the watchme above is emitted against it. Still open underneath: nothing yet READS that trail on a cadence — the measurement is available and un-taken, which is a weaker and more honest edge than the one it replaces.

THE REPORT IS A LAUNCH-TIME SNAPSHOT. It rides --append-system-prompt, so it persists for the whole session even after the floor is repaired mid-session. Acceptable today because it says it was measured at launch; a stale claim in a long session is the failure mode to watch.

SCOPE RULED OUT BY AKIEN, NOT FORGOTTEN: verifying and repairing the OTHER host-seams at launch (postgres reachable, sudo_relay up, bwrap present for the tester's isolation). The preflight's shape takes them without redesign — each is another finding appended by verify.
watchme_superseded: NONE, BECAUSE the residual question is not measurable from class-space, and the honest answer is to say so rather than to spec a watch that cannot be emitted. What this seam raises over time is: does a floor that was REPORTED broken actually get FIXED — i.e. does the report reaching Claude close the loop Akien named? That question is answered only by launch records in instance-space (~/.cairn/logs/preflight.json), and the probe berthing doctrine's destination (ii) — an instance-space probe — remains authored doctrine with NO WORKED EXAMPLE (filed by watchme-emits-a-probe, 2026-07-30). Carrying a watch I cannot emit would be exactly the silence the emission gate exists to refuse, wearing a spec's clothes. Two things kept this from becoming an excuse: the ONE residual question that WAS answerable from class-space — 'does the declared dependency set stay true as imports are added?' — was made PHYSICS instead of a watch (test_every_third_party_import_is_declared), because a watch on a question you can already answer is waiting to learn what you could measure; and the instance-space edge is filed below rather than dropped.
watchme_prose:
PROSE PRECURSOR to the spec above, kept because it is the reasoning the spec was compiled from — with ONE CLAIM CORRECTED rather than quietly swapped. It said this was 'probe berthing destination (ii)'s FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE — an instance-space probe'. THAT IS WRONG, and the way it is wrong is instructive: it reasoned from where the DATA lives (the boot log is in ~/.cairn/, never in git). The rule in cairn/tools/base/probe.py sorts on WHAT IS WATCHED, and what is watched here is the LAUNCHER'S DESIGN — the tool, which every install of this repo gets and every install needs working. So it is destination (i): checked in at launchers/probes/reported_but_unfixed_floor.py, beside the code it watches. Reading instance-space from a class-space berth is not an exception; it is the ordinary shape probe.py describes, where the predicate CLOSES OVER host-local data so only the poke crosses. THE TELL that (ii) was wrong: an instance-space berth is an absolute path in a ticket's spec, so the WATCHME gate would red on every other box that cloned the commons. A rule that places a probe where the gate cannot follow has not placed it. 

The rest stands: launchers/bootstrap.sh + launchers/superclaude write every launch to ~/.cairn/logs/boot through bin/logger_for_bash — what was probed and what came back (`verify:`), every repair attempted with its rc + output (`apply:`), each finding that SURVIVED apply (`report: unfixed —`), the cost, and the final `exec:` line. It SUPERSEDES the 'NONE, BECAUSE' this ticket carried, which was correct when written: the probe genuinely could not be emitted, because there was nothing to emit it WITH. Akien named the missing piece the same day — 'the WATCHME should be INSIDE of the superclaude script... it should log what the script tried, what worked, what didn't' — and building bin/logger_for_bash is what turned an honest refusal into a satisfiable summons.
